predecessors.name: Uruk period
predecessors.text: the southern alluvium around Uruk, where the Uruk-period culture gives way to Cliopatria's first city-state row

successors.name: Akkadian Empire
successors.text: Sumer: 'In his conquest of Sumer circa 2300 BC, Sargon of Akkad' took Uruk, Ur and Umma and 'laid waste' the land from Lagash to the sea

ledger.x: 3400 BCE: the first city-states form around Uruk.
3200 BCE: the cities multiply in the Jemdet Nasr stage.
2750 BCE: the kingship is at Kish.
2700 BCE: 'about thirteen independent cities' of Early Dynastic II–III.
2520 BCE: Lagash becomes a kingdom of its own under Ur-Nanshe ('r. c.
2500 BCE: the hegemony passes to Ur.
2425 BCE: Eannatum's hegemony lapses and the plain returns to the collective, now led from Uruk.
2340 BCE: the hold on Ur becomes Lugal-zage-si's annexation; Ur ends as a state (the gain two events below).
2340 BCE: the hold on Kish becomes annexation.
2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si 'annexed most of the territory of Lagash under king Urukagina'.
2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si 'invaded Kish, where he overthrew Ur-Zababa'.
2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si 'took Uruk and Ur, and made Uruk his capital'.
2340 BCE: Umma's ensi Lugal-zage-si 'established his new capital' at Uruk and Umma becomes a city of the collective's last kingdom.
2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si of Umma unites Sumer from Uruk.
2300 BCE: Sargon of Akkad conquers Sumer.

wars.name: Lagash–Umma border conflict
wars.outcome: Eannatum defeated Ush of Umma (Stele of the Vultures, c.

wars.name: Eannatum's campaigns
wars.outcome: Lagash 'conquered all of Sumer', overran parts of Elam and took tribute from Mari; the conquests lapsed at Eannatum's death (Kish 'regained its independence after his death').

wars.name: Lugal-zage-si's conquest of Sumer
wars.outcome: Umma's ensi took Lagash, Uruk, Ur, Kish, Nippur and Larsa and ruled Sumer from Uruk; no outer border moved (the raid to the 'upper sea' held no land, 'a successful raiding party').

wars.name: Sargon's conquest of Sumer
wars.outcome: Sargon 'defeated the city of Uruk and tore down its walls', 'was victorious over Ur in battle, conquered the city and destroyed its wall', led Lugal-zage-si 'in a neck-stock to Enlil's temple in Nippur' and annexed Sumer.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line anywhere: the cities were 'separated by canals and boundary stones' (Early Dynastic page), and the outer edge toward the steppe, the Zagros and the Gulf (whose coast then 'nearly reached Ur') is approximate.
